LMT_2017q2.summary_analysis: Two Dow Jones Newswires company-specific stories cover Lockheed Martin's first-quarter 2017 results, reported April 25. The company posted earnings of $763 million, or $2.61 per share, down from $898 million, or $2.91 per share, a year earlier, while revenue rose 6.6% to $11.1 billion; one article puts the shortfall against Wall Street at $2.79 per share on $11.23 billion of expected sales. Results were dented by nearly $200 million (39 cents per share) in charges tied to two Middle East programs -- a new UAE missile-defense system and an Abu Dhabi aircraft-maintenance joint venture -- which ended a run of quarters in which Lockheed had beaten forecasts. Despite the charges, Lockheed raised its full-year sales and cash-flow guidance while trimming per-share earnings guidance by 10 cents, to a new range of $12.15 to $12.45 on sales of $49.5 billion to $50.7 billion. International sales were 27% of revenue against a 30% target, and CEO Marillyn Hewson said she still expected both Middle East ventures to become growth opportunities. The aeronautics segment, the company's largest, grew sales 8%, driven largely by F-35 fighter jet volumes, and management reiterated expectations for continued F-35 margin expansion as it works to cut the jet's unit cost toward $80 million.
LMT_2017q2.why_moved: Both articles tie the share decline to the quarter falling short of Wall Street's profit and revenue expectations, driven by the nearly $200 million of Middle East-related charges.
